content:
# Judith Chapter 11 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Judith 11 (23 verses)
**Theme:** Judith's speech before Holofernes — double-truth deception

---

## Disagreement Count: 19

---

### Disagreement 1 — Verse 2: "despised" vs. "scorned" vs. "insulted"

**EMET:** "despised me"
**LOGOS:** "despised me"
**PNEUMA:** "insulted me"

**Issue:** The Greek exouthenesantes carries connotations of treating someone as nothing, despising them with contempt. PNEUMA opts for "insulted" (more active, interpersonal). EMET/LOGOS prefer "despised" (more weighty, attitudinal).
**SOPHIA ruling:** "Despised" retained — the word connotes treating someone as worthless, not merely a verbal insult.

---

### Disagreement 2 — Verse 3: Address format

**EMET:** Direct address embedded in a sentence
**LOGOS:** Presents as a sequence of questions and reassurances
**PNEUMA:** Breaks into shorter sentences for rhetorical impact

**Issue:** Holofernes' speech in vv. 1-4 is a single long period in Greek. How much to break it up?
**SOPHIA ruling:** Modest paragraph breaks preserved; the formal, speech-act quality of Holofernes' welcome kept intact.

---

### Disagreement 3 — Verse 7: Oath formula extent

**EMET:** Renders the oath formula in full with subordinate clauses intact
**LOGOS:** Same
**PNEUMA:** Condenses: "I swear by the life of Nebuchadnezzar... he who sent you to restore order"

**Issue:** The Greek oath formula is elaborate. PNEUMA condenses it without losing meaning; EMET/LOGOS preserve the formal-legal structure.
**SOPHIA ruling:** Full structure preserved — the legal weight of the oath is theologically meaningful.

---

### Disagreement 4 — Verse 7: "set every living soul in order" vs. "the setting right of every living soul" vs. "restore order among all living creatures"

**EMET:** "for the setting right of every living soul"
**LOGOS:** "to set every living person in order"
**PNEUMA:** "to restore order among all living creatures"

**Issue:** Greek eis epanorthōsin pasēs psychēs. The word psychē can be "soul," "person," or "living creature." EMET is most literal. LOGOS clarifies as "person." PNEUMA expands to "living creatures" (anticipating v. 7c about animals).
**SOPHIA ruling:** "To set every living person in order" — focuses the verse's primary reference on humans while not excluding the animal extension in the next clause.

---

### Disagreement 5 — Verse 8: "clever devices" vs. "skill of your mind" vs. "extraordinary cunning"

**EMET:** "the clever devices of your soul"
**LOGOS:** "the skill of your mind"
**PNEUMA:** "your mind's extraordinary cunning"

**Issue:** Greek panourgia (lit. "all-working" or "readiness for anything") — can be rendered neutrally as skill, or with the tinge of craftiness. Ironic that Judith, the true craftsperson of this story, uses this word about Holofernes.
**SOPHIA ruling:** "The cunning of your mind" — preserves the slight irony without being pejorative.

---

### Disagreement 6 — Verse 10: "lay it up in your heart" vs. "take it to heart" vs. "hold them close"

**EMET:** "lay it up in your heart"
**LOGOS:** "take it to heart"
**PNEUMA:** "hold them close"

**Issue:** Idiom vs. literalism. EMET preserves the Semitic idiom. LOGOS and PNEUMA naturalize it.
**SOPHIA ruling:** "Hold it close to your heart" — a middle path retaining the idiom in modern English.

---

### Disagreement 7 — Verse 11: Nature of the "sin" seizing them

**EMET:** "sin has seized them, with which they will provoke their God"
**LOGOS:** "sin has gripped them by which they will provoke their God"
**PNEUMA:** "Sin has seized them by the throat. They are about to do what will drive their God to fury."

**Issue:** PNEUMA adds "by the throat" as an interpretive expansion not in the Greek. Vivid but unauthorized.
**SOPHIA ruling:** "Sin has taken hold of them, by which they will provoke their God to anger." PNEUMA's addition rejected as going beyond the text.

---

### Disagreement 8 — Verse 12: "resolved to lay hands on their cattle"

**EMET:** "they resolved to lay hands upon their cattle"
**LOGOS:** "they resolved to lay hands on their livestock"
**PNEUMA:** "they made a decision: they would slaughter their livestock"

**Issue:** "Lay hands on" vs. "slaughter" — the Greek implies seizure/appropriation rather than necessarily slaughter. PNEUMA interprets too narrowly.
**SOPHIA ruling:** "Resolved to lay hands on their livestock" — the ambiguity preserved.

---

### Disagreement 9 — Verse 13: "firstfruits" terminology

**EMET:** "firstfruits of the grain"
**LOGOS:** "firstfruits of the grain"
**PNEUMA:** "The firstfruits of the grain"

**Issue:** All three agree on "firstfruits" — no disagreement here. Consensus achieved independently.
**Note:** Logged for completeness; unanimous agreement.

---

### Disagreement 10 — Verse 13: Who may not touch the consecrated things

**EMET:** "which it is not lawful for any of the people even to touch with their hands"
**LOGOS:** "which no member of the people may even touch with their hands"
**PNEUMA:** "Things no ordinary Israelite may even touch"

**Issue:** "Ordinary Israelite" (PNEUMA) slightly reframes — implying priests may touch, which is true but adds an interpretive layer. EMET's "it is not lawful" is more legalistic.
**SOPHIA ruling:** "which no member of the people may even touch with their hands" — clear, complete, literal enough.

---

### Disagreement 11 — Verse 14: "gerousia" rendering

**EMET:** "council of elders"
**LOGOS:** "senate"
**PNEUMA:** "the council of elders"

**Issue:** See SOPHIA council notes. "Senate" imports Roman political associations; "council of elders" is more transparent.
**SOPHIA ruling:** "Council of elders."

---

### Disagreement 12 — Verse 15: Sequence of events

**EMET:** "when the word comes back to them and they do it"
**LOGOS:** "when the word returns to them and they act upon it"
**PNEUMA:** "The moment that authorization arrives and they act on it"

**Issue:** PNEUMA adds "authorization" — technically the referent, but not in the text. Slightly over-explains.
**SOPHIA ruling:** "When the word comes back to them and they act upon it."

---

### Disagreement 13 — Verse 16: "things that will astound all the earth"

**EMET:** "things that will astound all the earth — as many as will hear about them"
**LOGOS:** "things that will astonish all the earth — as many as hear of them"
**PNEUMA:** "things that will leave the whole earth stunned — everyone who hears of it"

**Issue:** Minor: "astound" vs. "astonish" vs. "leave stunned." PNEUMA restructures the relative clause.
**SOPHIA ruling:** "Things that will astonish all the earth — everyone who hears of them." Small update for naturalness.

---

### Disagreement 14 — Verse 17: "God-fearing" vs. "devout"

**EMET:** "your servant is devout"
**LOGOS:** "your servant is God-fearing"
**PNEUMA:** "I am a woman who fears God"

**Issue:** Greek theosebes. EMET renders as general piety; LOGOS as the specific compound adjective. PNEUMA expands into a phrase.
**SOPHIA ruling:** "Your servant is God-fearing" — the compound renders the Greek compound precisely.

---

### Disagreement 15 — Verse 18: Army description

**EMET:** "your whole army"
**LOGOS:** "your entire army"
**PNEUMA:** "your full army"

**Issue:** All synonymous. Minor register variation.
**SOPHIA ruling:** "Your entire army."

---

### Disagreement 16 — Verse 19: "Not a dog will open its mouth"

**EMET:** "not a dog will open its mouth before you"
**LOGOS:** "not a dog will open its mouth before you"
**PNEUMA:** "not a dog will so much as growl in your direction"

**Issue:** PNEUMA's "growl" is a reasonable interpretation (a dog opening its mouth might bark or growl), but the literal phrase is more powerful as an echo of Exodus 11:7.
**SOPHIA ruling:** Literal phrase retained — the Exodus echo is intentional and should not be smoothed away.

---

### Disagreement 17 — Verse 21: Description of Judith

**EMET:** "so fair in face and so wise in words"
**LOGOS:** "so beautiful of face and so wise of speech"
**PNEUMA:** "not for beauty, not for wisdom"

**Issue:** PNEUMA condenses the direct quote into reported speech, losing the rhetorical balance. EMET/LOGOS preserve the paired adjectives.
**SOPHIA ruling:** "So beautiful of face and so wise in speech" — the balance of the original preserved.

---

### Disagreement 18 — Verse 22: Rendering of "despised/held in contempt"

**EMET:** "those who have despised my lord"
**LOGOS:** "those who have held my lord in contempt"
**PNEUMA:** "those who defied my lord"

**Issue:** "Defied" (PNEUMA) implies active resistance; "despised/contemned" implies an attitude of scorn. Greek athetesantes = "rejected, treated as void."
**SOPHIA ruling:** "Those who have held my lord in contempt" — captures the attitudinal scorn.

---

### Disagreement 19 — Verse 23: "renowned/celebrated throughout all the earth"

**EMET:** "renowned throughout all the earth"
**LOGOS:** "celebrated throughout all the earth"
**PNEUMA:** "your fame will spread over all the earth"

**Issue:** The irony is enormous: Holofernes promises Judith exactly what God will give her — world-renowned fame — but for the opposite reason. All three capture this but with different registers.
**SOPHIA ruling:** "Celebrated throughout all the earth" — the word "celebrated" carries the intended irony (celebrated in song, as she will indeed be in ch. 16).

---

## Summary

Total disagreements: 19
Major doctrinal issues: 0
Major translation choices: v. 7 (oath formula extent), v. 14 (gerousia), v. 16 (Exodus echo in v. 19), v. 17 (theosebes)
Key irony noted: Holofernes' promises in vv. 22-23 are all fulfilled — but not in the way he means.
